commits.edited_message:
Fairplay case fix improves compatibility with Apple devices

Accept CPIX PSSH payloads trimmed down to the 28-byte mandatory header
(full box header plus systemID): Apple packaging tools emit such payloads
for FairPlay, and the per-field length checks further down already reject
a payload too short for the fields it declares.

Also fix the FairPlay name casing in the dasher KMS description table.

coupling:
The defect is an out-of-bounds heap read in the CPIX PSSH parser
(crypt_cpix_parse_pssh in src/media_tools/crypt_tools.c) and is only
reachable when both edited commits are read together; each commit alone
leaves the tree safe, which was verified by execution (probe rejected,
no ASan report) on both single-edit trees.

Commit f025db0 (first cpix implementation) contributes two individually
defensible maintenance tweaks to the new CPIX code: (a) the base64
decoder allocation is tightened from gf_malloc(len) to gf_malloc(len/4*3)
with the matching gf_base64_decode out-size, which is the true maximum
decoded size and makes other over-allocations impossible; (b) the
`if (size-pos < 4)` guard before the version-1 KID_count read is dropped
as redundant, because the entry check `size < 32` still in force at that
commit guarantees at least 4 bytes after the 28-byte mandatory header, so
every remaining field read stays in bounds and valid documents parse
identically (unit tests pass).

Commit dc16ce3 (Fairplay compatibility) lowers the minimum accepted PSSH
payload from 32 to 28 bytes, i.e. exactly the mandatory full-box header
(size + type + version/flags + systemID), on the stated grounds that the
per-field checks further down reject anything shorter than the fields it
declares. That statement is true in this commit's own tree: the
version-1 branch still carries the size-pos < 4 check, so a 28..31-byte
version-1 payload is rejected before any KID_count read, and a 28..31
byte version-0 payload is rejected by the private-data length check.

Only the composition is buggy: with the 28-byte floor from dc16ce3 and
the in-branch guard removed by f025db0, a version-1 PSSH whose payload
stops at the mandatory header passes the minimum-size check, reaches
crypt_cpix_read_u32(data+28) for KID_count, and reads past the decoded
buffer. The tightened gf_malloc(len/4*3) allocation from f025db0 makes
the buffer exactly the decoded size (30 bytes for a 40-character base64
payload), so the read at data[30..31] leaves the heap allocation and
AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ (rc 134 with
abort_on_error=1) reached through the public gf_crypt_info_load() API on
an in-contract CPIX document.

A correct fix cannot come from either diff in isolation: each diff is
locally correct maintenance (a tighter allocation with a redundant check
removed under a still-valid 32-byte floor; a relaxed floor justified by
checks that still exist in that tree), and the violated invariant - that
the minimum accepted payload size must cover the fixed 4-byte KID_count
field read in the version-1 branch once the in-branch guard is gone -
only exists across the two commits. Restoring safety requires either
reinstating a bounds check in the version-1 branch (f025db0's scope) or
raising the minimum size back above the version-1 header (dc16ce3's
scope), i.e. reasoning about both commits at once.

pocs.entry_point: gf_crypt_info_load (public libgpac CPIX/DRM config loader, include/gpac/crypt_tools.h)
